content.title: About
content.content: A tart is an open‑topped pastry with a filling, typically made from a dough of flour, butter and eggs. Tarts can be sweet (fruit, berries, custard) or savory (vegetables, meat, cheese). The crust is often shortcrust, puff pastry or yeasted dough, and the filling is prepared separately and placed on the pre‑baked base.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tarts originated in France in the 17th century and quickly spread across Europe.
The word “tart” comes from the Old French “tarte”, meaning a flat pie.
The most famous sweet version is the Tarte Tatin, where apples are caramelised under the pastry and then flipped.
Savory tarts are commonly served as appetizers or light meals, especially in Mediterranean cuisine.
Gluten‑free tart crusts can be made using rice or almond flour.

items.title: Rich source of energy
items.content: Tarts provide carbohydrates and fats that supply quick energy.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fruit‑filled sweet tarts deliver vitamin C, potassium and fibre, while savory versions contribute iron and calcium from cheese and meat.

items.title: Protein in savory varieties
items.content: Tarts with meat, fish or legumes are good sources of animal or plant protein.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet tarts can contain a lot of added sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or weight management.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Butter‑based crusts are high in saturated fats and should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Tarts often contain gluten, dairy, nuts or eggs – common allergens.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tarts can be served warm or cold. Sweet versions are often paired with whipped cream, ice cream or berry sauce. Savory tarts are sliced into portions and enjoyed with a salad or dipping sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a finished tart in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze it tightly wrapped for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven before serving to restore a crisp crust.
